findings.description: Video ref callback uses undefined variable `i` — map callback is `(media)` with no index param, so `videoRefs.current[i]` always writes to `videoRefs.current[undefined]`. No video element is ever stored; entire play/pause/reset logic is a silent no-op. Fix: change `(media)` to `(media, i)`.

Fetch has no AbortController cleanup. On fast unmount the .then() callbacks still fire and call setBlogsData/setIsLoading on an unmounted component. Fix: create AbortController, pass signal to fetch, abort in useEffect cleanup return.

Dead import: `sentenceCase` is imported from `../utils/text` but never called in config.js. The `position` field is a plain string literal and summary[] templates it directly without invoking sentenceCase. Remove the import.

No `environment: 'jsdom'` in vitest config. Tests run in Node with manual global stubs for `document` and `localStorage`. Adding jsdom lets tests use real DOM APIs and eliminates fragile manual stub objects.

`totalExperiences` arithmetic (`format(new Date(),'yyyy') - careerSince - 1`) has zero test coverage. A wrong year would silently display the wrong experience count with no build or lint error to catch it.

`next` pinned at 13.0.2 (Oct 2022) has multiple disclosed CVEs from 2024-2025 (CVE-2024-34351, CVE-2024-46982, CVE-2025-29927 among others). Upgrading to 13.5.x preserves the same Pages Router API surface with minimal risk.
`eslint` (8.27.0) and `eslint-config-next` (13.0.2) are listed in `dependencies` instead of `devDependencies`. These are build/lint tools with no runtime use. Move both to devDependencies.
`eslint` 8.27.0 reached end-of-life in 2024 and will not receive security fixes. The current stable is ESLint 9. `eslint-config-next` should be bumped alongside Next.js.
`@vercel/analytics` capped at ^1.0.1; latest is 2.0.1 with breaking API changes (`inject()` removed, `Analytics` component API changed). Review changelog before bumping.

`@emailjs/browser` capped at ^3.9.1; latest is 4.4.1. v4 changed `send`/`sendForm` return type and the public key is now a required third argument to `emailjs.init()`. Audit Contact.jsx usage before upgrading.

Blog thumbnail `<Image>` uses hardcoded `width={500} height={500}` for all cards regardless of actual image dimensions. This can distort non-square thumbnails and prevents accurate Next.js image optimisation. Consider `fill` layout with a sized container.

No guard on `data.items` before calling `.forEach()`. If rss2json returns an error-shaped response, `data.items` is undefined and throws an uncaught TypeError, leaving isLoading stuck at true. Add a guard before the loop.
Field name typo: `commentor` (misspelling) propagates into Blog.jsx at `singleData?.commentor`. Rename to `author` in both AllBlogData.js and Blog.jsx as a coordinated change.

`AllBlogData` is a custom React hook (calls useState/useEffect) but does not follow the `use*` naming convention. ESLint hooks rules cannot identify it as a hook. Rename to `useAllBlogData` and update the caller in ContextProvider.js.
File named `UseData.js` with function `UseData` (Pascal-case). All other hooks use lowercase `use*`. Rename file to `useData.js` and export to `useData`. Update import in Blog.jsx.
`forEach` + mutable `items` accumulator pattern should be replaced with `data.items.map(...)`. More idiomatic, avoids intermediate mutation, signals intent clearly.

`heroContent` is a module-level object that only re-names imported values under different keys (heroImage, heroTitleName, etc.). Pure indirection with zero benefit. Remove the object and reference imported values directly in JSX.

Summary paragraphs use the sentence text as React key (`key={description}`). Long strings are fragile keys; duplicated sentences would silently break reconciliation. Use the array index instead (list is static and never reordered).

Twitter card meta tags use `property=` (Open Graph convention) instead of the correct `name=` attribute. Per Twitter/X docs, Twitter tags must use `<meta name="twitter:*">`. Scrapers may miss the card with wrong attribute.

Theme toggle uses `onClick` on a checkbox `<input>` instead of `onChange`. The checkbox has no `checked` prop (uncontrolled), so browser checked state and React `isLightTheme` state diverge. Make it controlled (`checked={isLightTheme} onChange={...}`) or switch to a `<button>`.

`localStorage` accessed inside `useEffect` without `typeof window !== 'undefined'` guard. Currently safe since useEffect is client-only, but fragile if this code is ever moved outside useEffect. Add the guard for explicitness.

`safelyResetRecaptcha` catch block is empty (`catch (_) {}`), silently swallowing all errors. Add a `console.warn` to preserve silent-recovery intent while making debugging reCAPTCHA edge cases possible.

Modal backdrop `<div>` has an onClick handler but no `role="button"` or `aria-label`. Keyboard users and screen readers cannot dismiss the modal via the backdrop. Add `role="button" aria-label="Close modal"` or convert to `<button>`.

Modal has no focus trap. When the portal opens, focus stays on the trigger; Tab cycles through the underlying page behind the overlay. Use native `inert` attribute, a `<dialog>` element, or a manual keydown trap.
No Escape key handler on the modal. Add a `useEffect` that registers a `keydown` listener for `event.key === 'Escape'` calling `handleClose`, cleaned up on unmount.

Portal root `<div className="modal_portfolio">` is missing `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, and `aria-labelledby` pointing at the `<h2>`. Without these, assistive technologies do not announce it as a dialog.

`personSchema` is built at module load time (top-level, outside component). For a static site this is harmless, but if `siteURL` resolves from an env var differing between server/client, the schema could embed the wrong URL. Consider memoizing inside the component.
Mobile hero `<Image>` is missing the `priority` prop. This image is the largest-contentful-paint candidate on mobile viewports. Add `priority` to eliminate the lazy-load penalty on first paint.

`Aos.init({ duration: 1200 })` sets a default, but individual elements across the codebase also hardcode `data-aos-duration="1200"`. The per-element overrides are redundant. Remove them and let the init default govern all elements.

Portfolio card `<Image>` elements in the first tab are loaded lazily (default). The first few cards above the fold could benefit from `priority` to improve LCP. Add `priority` to the first 2-3 images of the active tab.

The `skillSets` array with all skill icon imports is defined inside the component body and reallocated on every render. It is entirely static data. Move it to module scope, consistent with how `experienceContent` and `educationContent` are handled in sibling files.

Tests stub `global.document` and `global.localStorage` with plain objects. Once jsdom is configured (f-0004), these manual stubs can be replaced with `vi.spyOn` on real DOM methods, which is more resilient and realistic.

Missing edge-case tests for `handleSwitchValue`: null/undefined/0/'' inputs (all falsy, should apply light theme), verifying localStorage key is always 'theme-color', and verifying add is called before remove.
Zero test coverage for hooks: `useBodyScrollLock`, `useExpandableList`, and `useData`. `useExpandableList` and `useBodyScrollLock` are pure enough to test without a full component harness.

The video ref bug (f-0001) has no test coverage. The play/pause logic is the only non-trivial stateful behaviour in the modal. A test checking ref population and the play/pause effect would have caught the silent breakage.

`date-fns` at ^2.30.0; latest is v4.4.0. v4 is ESM-only and dropped CJS — Next 13.0.2 may need `transpilePackages` in next.config.js. Usage: `format` in config.js and `format`+`parseISO` in AllBlogData.js. Likely safe but needs verification.

`react-toastify` at 9.1.3; latest is 11.1.0. v10/v11 changed the default `position` type from string to an enum constant and altered some prop names. The `position: "top-right"` in config.js may need updating.
`react-animated-cursor` installed at 2.6.0 but latest within ^2.5.2 range is 2.11.2 — 5 minor versions behind. Visual/behavioural regressions are possible; manual cursor test needed before shipping.
Medium RSS feed URL hardcoded inside the hook. The `mediumURL` already lives in config.js; the feed URL should be derived there too. A username change currently requires updating two separate files.

Blog items use array index as `id`. If the RSS feed returns fewer items (post unpublished), indices shift and stale `singleData` can point to the wrong post. Use `item.guid` (already stored as `link`) as a stable identifier.

Restores `document.body.style.overflow` to `''` (empty string) on cleanup. If another element set overflow before the modal opened, closing it clears that value. Capture the existing value on mount and restore it exactly on cleanup.

`MyContext` is a generic name. With one context it is fine, but adding a second would immediately collide. Rename to `BlogContext` to reflect what it actually holds. Depends on renaming AllBlogData (f-0014) first.

Contact `TabTitle` hard-codes the string `"contact"` as the `bg` prop instead of using `menuLabels.contact`. Every other TabTitle uses menuLabels. A label rename would silently leave the contact background watermark out of sync.

`SocialShare` array is module-level config data defined inside a presentational component file. It belongs in config.js alongside other personal data (github, linkedin, etc.) for a single source of truth.

Multiple commented-out `// 'status': 1` fields across entries — dead scaffolding from an unimplemented feature. If not planned, remove. If planned, add a JSDoc comment explaining the intended values (1=live, 2=discontinued?).

Several `preview` arrays have commented-out entries (discontinued live site URLs). Fine as a historical record but adds noise to a large data file. Remove or move to a `legacyUrls` field if preservation matters.

`dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: singleData?.description }}` — when `singleData.description` is absent, optional chaining returns undefined and `__html: undefined` renders the string "undefined" in some browsers. Guard with `|| ''`.
`` uses next/image for a local SVG. Per CLAUDE.md, next/image cannot render raw SVGs without dangerouslyAllowSVG (blocked). Replace with a plain `` tag.

Component function is named `index` (lowercase default export). React DevTools displays it as `index` instead of a meaningful name. Rename the function to `About` — the file name does not need to change.
Empty template literals (`link: ```) used as falsy guards. Plain `link: ''` is cleaner and avoids visual noise of unnecessary template literals with no interpolation.
`val.details ? ... : null` and `val.link ? ... : null` use ternary instead of the `&&` short-circuit pattern used everywhere else in the codebase for conditional renders. Use `&&` for consistency.

Three separate `useState` calls (`getModal`, `modalCategory`, `modalProject`) are always set together in `handleModal`. Collapse into a single `useState(null)` holding `{ category, project }` or `null` when closed.
Trailing `{" "}` after the PortfolioModal conditional render is unnecessary whitespace noise. Remove it.

The rejection handler (`() => {}`) in the `.then(onFulfilled, onRejected)` pattern silently swallows the error object. At minimum log it with `console.error` to make debugging failed fetches possible.

`siteURL` fallback chain includes `process.env.SITE_URL`, a server-only env var not available in the browser bundle. Since config.js is imported by Seo.jsx (client-rendered), this branch is always undefined on the client — it is dead code on the client side. Remove the `|| process.env.SITE_URL` fallback from config.js (keep it only in next-sitemap.config.js where it is server-only).
Role tags use the tag string as React key (`key={tag}`). Same fragility as summary keys (f-0018). Use the array index for this static, never-reordered list.
The component return wraps `<Head>` in an unnecessary `<> </>` fragment. `<Head>` is the only child; remove the outer fragment.
`<meta httpEquiv="x-ua-compatible" content="ie=edge">` targets Internet Explorer (end-of-life). All supported browsers ignore this tag. Remove it.

The `pageTitle` fallback (`pageTitle ? ... : metaTitle`) is unreachable dead code — the only caller (`home-dark.jsx`) always passes a truthy value. Either remove the prop and hardcode `metaTitle` or document the fallback is intentional for future callers.
Contact panel copy escapes apostrophes using JSX string literals (`{"LET'S"}`, `{"you'd"}`). Inconsistent with the rest of the file. Use curly-quotes or Unicode characters directly.
The `return` wraps everything in an unnecessary `<> </>` fragment — `<form>` is the only child. Remove the outer fragment.
Subject field uses `col-12 col-md-12` — `col-md-12` is redundant because `col-12` already makes the element full width at all breakpoints. Use just `col-12`.

`handleSwitchValue(!nextIsLight)` double negation is confusing: `nextIsLight=true` means switching to light, passes `false`. The logic is correct but the inverted argument makes intent opaque. Add a clarifying comment or rename the variable.
Social links use `rel="noreferrer"` which implicitly includes `noopener` in modern browsers, but `rel="noopener noreferrer"` is more explicit and consistent for external links.
404 page hard-codes `"Page Not Found | Myo Win Thein"` in the title instead of using `firstName`/`lastName` from config.js. A name change would require updating the 404 title separately.
Description paragraphs use text content as React key. If two paragraphs ever share the same text, this causes a key collision. Use array index instead (list is static and never reordered).

Project card `<div>` has `onClick` but no `role="button"`, `tabIndex={0}`, or `onKeyDown` handler. Keyboard users cannot activate cards via Enter/Space. Convert to `<button>` or add the missing ARIA attributes and key handler.

Bullet points rendered as `•   {text}` inside `

` tags mix content and formatting. Using `

    `/`
  • ` (already used for the outer list) with CSS-driven bullets would be more semantic.

Achievement items use `val.subTitle2` (e.g. 'experience', 'start') as React key. These are presentation labels, not identifiers. Silent collision if a second entry ever shares the same subtitle. Use index or add a dedicated `id`.
`handleSwitchValue` is a default export only. `utils/text.js` uses named exports. Convert to a named export (`export function handleSwitchValue`) for consistency and more explicit tree-shaking.
`date-fns` `format()` is imported just to call `format(new Date(), 'yyyy')`. Replace with the built-in `new Date().getFullYear()` and remove the only reason config.js depends on date-fns.

All 60+ skill SVG imports are at module level, adding their StaticImageData metadata to the module graph regardless of whether the user opens the About tab. Low risk at current scale but worth noting if bundle size becomes a concern.

All media items in AwesomeSlider render on modal open. Images use `<Image>` without `loading="lazy"`. For modals with 5-7 media items, all images are eagerly decoded. Add `loading="lazy"` to non-first-slide images.

reCAPTCHA script is appended in useEffect without checking for an existing script tag. During HMR the component can remount and add a duplicate script. Guard with a `document.querySelector('[src*=recaptcha]')` check before appending.

`sentenceCase` is missing tests for numeric string input (`'123abc'`) and already-sentence-case input (`'Hello world'` should return unchanged). Edge coverage is thin for a function used in SEO meta generation.

`useExpandableList` is a pure hook with clear input/output (initialCount, toggle, showAll state) and no DOM side effects. It is a natural candidate to add to the test suite alongside existing utils tests.

`react-tabs` at ^5.1.0 (installed 5.2.0); latest is 6.1.1. v6 dropped IE 11 support and changed `forceRenderTabPanel` default. Review before upgrading since react-tabs is the core navigation primitive in home-dark.jsx.
`react-awesome-slider` at ^4.1.0 has not had a release since 2021 and is effectively unmaintained. Works with React 18 but has no React 19 support — long-term risk if the project upgrades React.
`next-sitemap` at ^4.1.3 (installed 4.1.3); latest is 4.2.3. Safe patch-level bump within the same major — low risk to update.
`react-modal` at ^3.16.1 (installed 3.16.1); latest is 3.16.3. Two patch releases behind; safe to bump. Used in Blog.jsx.
`vitest` at ^4.1.9; minor patch update available. Safe to update.

Fetch chain uses .then(onFulfilled, onRejected) with no trailing .catch(). A synchronous exception thrown inside the success handler (item parsing) becomes an unhandled rejection instead of being caught by onRejected, leaving isLoading stuck true with no error toast. Add a final .catch(err => { toast.error(...); setIsLoading(false); }).

item.categories.join(', ') and format(parseISO(item.pubDate), ...) assume every feed item has well-formed categories/pubDate. A malformed item throws inside the map callback. Guard with (item.categories || []).join(', ') and validate pubDate before formatting.

No test exercises a malformed individual feed item (missing categories/description, invalid pubDate). Add a case asserting the hook still resolves isLoading to false / surfaces an error toast once f-0082's catch handler lands.

Tracking-pixel stripping is duplicated: a regex strip on 'medium.com/_/stat' at fetch time here, and a separate DOM-based strip in Blog.jsx's stripTrackingImages checking the same substring. If the pattern changes, both need updating. The DOM layer also catches generically-broken images so isn't purely redundant — consolidate or document why both exist.

singleData?.description (raw HTML from the Medium RSS feed via rss2json) is rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML with no sanitization. It's your own feed today, but unexpected markup from rss2json would render unsanitized in visitors' browsers.

Captures document.body.style.overflow as previousOverflow at mount and restores that exact value on unmount, with no shared lock counter. If two consumers ever lock concurrently, closing the first-opened one would unlock scroll while the second is still open. Currently safe only because the app enforces mutual exclusion elsewhere.

value = useAllBlogData() returns a freshly-constructed object every render, so BlogContext.Provider always gets a new reference. Wrapping the returned object in useMemo would avoid unnecessary reference churn for consumers doing reference-equality checks.

Directory names src/Hooks and src/Context are capitalized while every sibling directory (components, layout, pages, styles) is lowercase. A rename to hooks/, context/ would align the convention, but touches ~8 import paths across the codebase — worth confirming it's wanted before a mechanical but wide-reaching rename.

menuLabels is imported from ../../config but never referenced in the file — dead code left over from a prior version. next/core-web-vitals doesn't flag unused imports, so it silently ships. Remove the unused import.

45+ SVG icon imports and the 90-line skillSets data array live inside the About presentational component rather than a dedicated data module. The codebase already has a convention for this (portfolioData.js); extracting skillSets to a sibling aboutData.js would match that pattern.

useExpandableList(experienceContent, 3) uses an inline magic number for the initial visible count, while Skills.jsx extracts the equivalent into a named CORE_COUNT constant. Extracting a similarly named constant would make the two sibling components consistent.
The Laravel certificate link uses a template literal with no interpolation while every other entry in educationContent uses plain double-quoted strings. Convert to a plain string for consistency.

achievementsContent.map((val, i) => ... key={i}) uses the array index as key even though a stable unique value is already available (val.subTitle2). Harmless today since the list is static, but an easy mechanical fix.

No test exercises skillSets.length <= CORE_COUNT (e.g. exactly 4 groups) to confirm the toggle button renders sensibly with nothing extra to reveal, nor an empty skillSets array. Low-value given static data, but an uncovered branch.

modalProject.media.map assumes media is always a non-empty array with no guard (unlike preview, which is defensively checked with ?.length). All 17 current portfolioData entries supply media, but a future entry without it would throw or render an empty slider.

Every image in the AwesomeSlider gets identical alt text (modalProject.product), so a screen reader announces the same description for all 5+ screenshots. Would need a per-media alt/caption field in portfolioData.js to fix properly.

PortfolioModal is rendered without a React key in Portfolio.jsx; its internal state (activeIndex, videoRefs) only resets correctly because the parent always passes modal=null (unmount) between opening different projects. A future 'next/prev project' UX that skips that null gap would leak stale state.

Chance Myanmar's media array orders images as Img1, Img3, Img4, Img2, Img5 instead of sequential 1-5, unlike every other project entry. Likely an accidental reorder rather than intentional curation — worth confirming.

126 lines of hand-written static image imports (5-6 per project x 17 projects) with no shared helper or naming convention enforcement. next/image's requirement for literal static import paths limits how far this can be automated, but worth a lightweight convention check.

fastforwardImg4 is a .png while every other portfolio image (including the other 4 FastForward images) is .webp, breaking the otherwise consistent format convention. May be intentional if the source only exists as PNG.

The setInterval polling window.grecaptcha has no attempt ceiling or timeout. If the reCAPTCHA script never loads (blocked by an ad/privacy blocker), the interval runs every 150ms indefinitely with no feedback until the visitor tries to submit.

ensureSingleRecaptchaField (dedupe of duplicate g-recaptcha-response fields, fallback create-if-none-exists path) has no direct test coverage, even though its comment describes it as fixing a real prior bug (duplicate field breaking verification).

No test (or try/catch in source) covers localStorage.getItem/setItem throwing, which happens in Safari private browsing or when third-party storage is blocked; the effect and handleToggle would throw unhandled.

404 page builds its own bare <Head><title> instead of reusing the shared <SEO> component. It ships without the viewport meta tag, favicon link, canonical URL, and OG/Twitter tags every other page gets — the 404 page can render at desktop width on mobile and show no favicon.

The dynamically injected reCAPTCHA script has no onerror handler. If the script fails to load, Contact.jsx's grecaptcha polling loop has nothing to catch and the contact form silently never becomes submittable, with no user-facing error.
script.async = true and script.defer = true are both set; per spec async takes precedence when both are present, so defer is a no-op. Pick one attribute to avoid the confusing combination.
Only asserts tab-switch content for the Work and Contact tabs; the About and Blog TabPanels have no equivalent assertion that their content renders after the corresponding tab is clicked.

totalPlatformTypes (5) and totalDeliveredProjects (14) are hand-maintained magic numbers instead of being derived from portfolioData.js. The current count of 14 entries happens to match today, but nothing enforces they stay in sync as portfolio entries are added or removed.

metaTitle embeds a literal em dash (—) between name and position. This is user-facing copy (rendered as the SEO/browser-tab title) and conflicts with this project's own no-em-dash content convention; replace with a comma.

Both Poppins (6 weights) and Open Sans (4 weights) are configured with style: ['normal', 'italic'], generating/preloading 12 + 8 self-hosted font files. Poppins is only applied to headings which never use italic, and italic appears in only one CSS rule elsewhere — most italic variants are downloaded but never rendered.

sass and next-sitemap are build-time-only CLI tools with no runtime import anywhere in src/, but are listed under dependencies rather than devDependencies. Not currently breaking anything since Vercel installs devDependencies too, but the categorization is misleading.
